clue.text: Expectation of the man taking work on board

indicators.note: taking something means holding it within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the pronoun for a man
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone expects a man to take a job on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work on board' suggests a job on a ship, but 'on board' only reinforces that the work is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is a feeling of expectation that something wanted will happen.

clue.text: Weed round front of semi with instrument, gardening aid

indicators.note: one word goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: to hoe is to weed with a hoe

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of semi
a pipe is a simple wind instrument

explanation.surface: Weeding around a semi-detached house with a tool, a gardening job.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, but only its first letter is used here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosepipe is the flexible tube used for watering in the garden.

clue.text: Girl, aristocratic? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means it stops one letter short

parts.note: patrician means of noble birth

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a girl is truly upper-class: not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the final N of PATRICIAN leaves the girl's name PATRICIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricia is a common girl's name.

clue.text: Trying on red heels and short trousers

indicators.note: something trying is troublesome, suggesting letters put through a tiresome jumbling

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone tries on red high heels together with short trousers in a fitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying on' reads as a phrase about fitting clothes, but 'on' belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lederhosen are the traditional leather short trousers of Bavaria and Austria.

clue.text: Former cashier, we hear, in a royal treasury

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the spelling may differ from what is said

parts.note: a checker at a supermarket till handles payments

explanation.surface: An ex-cashier now works in the crown's treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: A checker is an American word for a checkout cashier; CHEQUER is spelt differently but sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government's treasury, historically the royal treasury.

clue.text: Follow unseen, mostly in disguise

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
something in disguise has its appearance changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Tail someone covertly, keeping mostly hidden in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards, as a result.

clue.text: Reportedly conceal Scottish explorer, with difficulty, in a West End location

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word is sound rather than spelling

parts.note: to hide is to conceal
Mungo Park explored the Niger River
to be in a corner is to be in difficulty

explanation.surface: A Scottish explorer is reportedly hidden away, with difficulty, somewhere in the West End.
explanation.walkthrough: Mungo Park was an 18th-century Scottish explorer of West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park Corner is a well-known junction at the western edge of London's West End.

clue.text: Famous lawgiver given good farewell

parts.note: Solon was the lawmaker of ancient Athens
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A celebrated lawgiver is given a fine send-off.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So long' is an informal way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Kind disposition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind disposition' reads as a gentle temperament; 'Kind' is a noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature means both the sort of thing something is and a person's inborn character.

clue.text: Highly amused, choose the odd tale to be broadcast

parts.note: to tick an option on a form is to choose it

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone delighted picks a strange story to go out on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be broadcast' suggests radio and a sound-alike, but it means scattered, and 'odd' is part of the letters, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickled to death is an idiom for extremely pleased or amused.

clue.text: Ready examples of rehearsed moves

parts.note: set means prepared, as in 'ready, steady, go'
pieces are specimens or examples, as in pieces of work

explanation.surface: A list of ready-made examples of practised routines, like a coach's notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: Set pieces are planned, practised moves, as at free kicks and corners in football.

clue.text: Dexterous lady primarily brought in to make earthenware

indicators.note: a thing brought in is placed inside the other word

parts.note: deft means skilful with the hands

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the first letter of lady

explanation.surface: A skilled woman is called in to throw some pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white glazed earthenware named after the Dutch town where it was made.

clue.text: Smart choice crossing river

indicators.note: one word spans across the other, straddling it on both sides

parts.note: the pick is the choice, as in pick of the bunch
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A clever choice of route that crosses a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective meaning clever, but it is the verb: to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart and to prick are both verbs for causing a sharp stinging pain.

clue.text: Look at key and wonder?

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
a key is something that opens a lock

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a key, puzzling over what it unlocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'wonder' is a noun here: a surprising revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising, revealing thing, which is a cause of wonder.

clue.text: Key issue in 2011, say

parts.note: key and prime both mean chief or most important
an issue of a magazine is a number

explanation.surface: A major problem arising in the year 2011.
explanation.walkthrough: '2011' looks like a date, but it is an example of a number divisible only by itself and one; 'say' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: 2011 has no divisors other than 1 and itself, so it is an example of such a figure.

clue.text: Onlooker before with rest shivering outside

parts.note: by means before, as in by noon

indicators.note: the shaken word sits outside the other one, wrapping it
shivering means trembling, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
and means together with

explanation.surface: An onlooker who stood earlier, now shivering while resting outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' looks like a synonym to replace, but its own letters are rearranged around AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander is a person present at an event who watches without taking part.

clue.text: Talk idly about award? It doesn't make any difference

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to natter is to chat idly
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Gossiping about an award changes nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British award given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No matter' is an idiom saying something is unimportant or irrelevant.

clue.text: How earth may be turned into an airport

indicators.note: turning one thing into another remodels it, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: How farmland can be dug up and converted to a runway.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is London's largest airport.

clue.text: A Muse could make poets richer

indicators.note: one thing could make another, so these letters are refashioned into a new word

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Inspiration from a Muse might bring poets wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Terpsichore is the Greek Muse of dance and choral song, one of the nine Muses.

clue.text: Size of a horse used for riding

parts.note: taken as written
a mount is a horse one rides

explanation.surface: Asking how big a riding horse is.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity or extent, the size of something.

clue.text: Bachelor by house, extremely drunk

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Bachelor, as in BA
house and lotto are both names for the game bingo

explanation.surface: A single man staggering past a house, very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: House (or housey-housey) is an old British name for bingo, also called lotto.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Play tune no end, hit by Armstrong originally

indicators.note: with no end means the final letter is cut off the word

parts.note: a melody is a tune
to ram is to hit forcefully

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Armstrong

explanation.surface: Instruction to play a tune endlessly, a hit by Louis Armstrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play tune' reads as a musical instruction, but 'Play' is the definition and 'hit' a verb, not a chart success.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage drama, a kind of play.

clue.text: Vessel from Kenya or Tanzania

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

parts.note: end of Kenya, all of or, start of Tanzania

explanation.surface: A ship sailing from an East African port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, a blood vessel.

clue.text: Respond emotionally about turn

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: Someone gets upset over a twist in events.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond, often with feeling, to something that happens.

clue.text: Extremist in Kabul, traitor

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the run of words that follows, spanning two of them

parts.note: the end of Kabul plus the start of traitor

explanation.surface: A militant in Afghanistan's capital is a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme political views.

clue.text: Special revolutionary character

parts.note: red is a common label for a revolutionary or communist
a character of the alphabet is a letter

explanation.surface: A distinctive figure who is a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special one, from saints' days printed in red in calendars.

clue.text: It may bring comfort to a child, receiving love if throaty, suffering

definitions.text: It may bring comfort to a child

indicators.note: a word receiving another takes it inside itself
something suffering is in a bad way, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A child with a sore throat is comforted by being given love.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a poorly child; the comfort is for a lost tooth instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The tooth fairy leaves a coin for a child's lost tooth, consoling them over the loss.

clue.text: Cold, and sore throat

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
raw skin is sore

explanation.surface: Symptoms of a winter illness: a chill and a painful throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sore throat' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Craw is an old word for the crop or throat, as in 'sticks in my craw'.
